summary: Return a small page of records from the selected layout or table.
purpose: Use this when you want to inspect a table or layout safely before doing anything more advanced.
learningGoals: Understand the difference between a Data API layout and an OData table.
Practice safe read-only pagination with a predictable limit.
See how the browser asks the protected PHP bridge to run a request.
explanation: This module gives beginners a safe first request. It keeps the browser on the same origin, avoids credentials in generated code, and shows the transport-specific shape for FileMaker reads.
commonMistakes: Using a table name while the Data API is selected.
Setting an extremely large limit before confirming the request works.
Assuming browser code should talk directly to FileMaker.
expectedResult: You get starter code that asks for a small page of records using either Data API or OData conventions.

prerequisites: Choose a FileMaker layout for Data API or a table for OData.
Keep the browser request routed through the authenticated PHP bridge.

inputs.label: Layout or table
inputs.help: Use the Data API layout name or the OData table name you want to read from.

inputs.label: How many records
inputs.help: Start small so your first test stays fast and easy to review.

beginner: List records is the safest first step because it reads without changing data.
The browser code talks only to the same-origin PHP bridge, not directly to FileMaker.
OData uses tables while the Data API uses layouts, so the label matters.
advanced: Use small limits first so fixture output and live smoke tests stay predictable.
The JavaScript variant mirrors the protected playground endpoint contract already used by the app.
The PHP template intentionally preserves the legacy starter output exactly.
